name: JSON View
summary: JSON View. Renders structured JSON as a collapsible, searchable tree with typed syntax color and selectable text.

lifecycle.compatibility: Available for controlled production evaluation; the contract may still be refined.
lifecycle.rationale: The structured-data tree remains beta while large-payload performance, controlled expansion, and manual assistive-technology evidence mature.
knownLimitations: The component intentionally renders read-only JSON-compatible values and does not provide inline editing or schema validation.
Consumers must paginate, summarize, or virtualize very large payloads before passing them to the component.
promotionCriteria: Public API, defaults, aliases and entrypoint ownership are reviewed.
SSR/hydration, keyboard, accessibility and visual evidence are linked.
Runtime scale limits and consumer testing contract are documented.
Migration impact is classified before lifecycle promotion.

api.name: data
api.description: JSON-compatible value rendered as an inspectable hierarchy.

api.name: ariaLabel
api.description: Accessible name announced for the JSON tree.

api.name: defaultExpandDepth
api.description: Number of hierarchy levels expanded when data first renders.

api.name: expandedPaths
api.description: Controlled JSON-pointer paths, or null to keep expansion state internal.

api.name: highlightPattern
api.description: Text or regular expression highlighted in visible keys and primitive values.

api.name: sortKeys
api.description: Sorts object keys with locale-aware comparison while preserving array order.

api.name: wrap
api.description: Allows long keys and values to wrap inside the viewport.

keyboard: Arrow Up and Arrow Down move the single roving focus through visible properties.
Arrow Right expands or enters a branch; Arrow Left collapses it or returns to its parent.
Home and End move to the first and last visible property; Enter or Space toggles a branch.
notes: The tree exposes each visible property's hierarchy, sibling position, and expansion state.
Keys and typed primitive values remain text, so syntax color is never the only representation.
Highlighting uses a visible mark treatment without replacing the underlying accessible text.
KERN avoids ambient browser globals in reusable runtime infrastructure.
Validate the consuming SSR/hydration route, locale, ids and overlay host.

examples.title: Inspectable deployment payload

guidance.useWhen: Use JSON View when users need to inspect structured application data while preserving hierarchy, value types, and copyable text.
guidance.avoidWhen: Use Code Block for an immutable source excerpt, and a purpose-built detail view when users must edit or act on individual fields.

commonMistakes: Importing from an undeclared family path or a source implementation file.
Loading only tokens.css instead of the complete styles/kern.css component bundle.
Assuming the documentation SSR build replaces validation of the consuming application.
checklist: Import the symbol from its documented owner entrypoint; do not use a deep source import.
Load @kern-ui/angular/styles/kern.css exactly once in the application's global styles.
Provide every required input and keep collection identities stable across updates.
Verify keyboard, focus, visible labels, invalid state, long text, RTL and 200% zoom.
Test the consuming SSR/hydration route when server rendering is enabled.
Use @kern-ui/angular/testing harnesses when a component-specific harness is available.

exclusions.reason: Low-value duplicate accessibility copy is validated by the a11y fixture and kept stable while visual parameters change.
The public type is not a lossless scalar/literal contract and requires a typed specimen fixture.
Collection and data-source inputs require typed identities and deterministic fixtures rather than scalar serialization.
